requirement_title: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly
requirement_text:
# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283
Type: bug

## Requirement

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with no generated resolver at all. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime.

Repro: two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`.

Expected: a clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.

Actual:

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`. Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8.

What triggers it (`Item` declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`):

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | crash |
| `struct Item<T>` | crash |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

It needs all three of: generic, value type, from a referenced assembly. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` makes the crash disappear.

Reporter's analysis: `CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly, so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` like the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers. That collection is empty for a metadata symbol. The reporter did not narrow down which of the three fires.

Workaround: `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` before `GetObjectInfo` is reached.

## Acceptance criteria

- Building `app` from the repro produces no CS8785 warning. (derived)
- Building `app` from the repro produces no AD0001 warning from `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer`. (derived)
- `app.dll` contains a `GeneratedMessagePackResolver` (a generated resolver exists). (derived)
- The generator and analyzer do not throw on a closed generic struct or record struct declared in a referenced assembly.
- Closed generic classes, non-generic structs and types declared in the same assembly keep working as before (the "ok" rows in the table). (derived)
- Diagnostics that need a source location do not crash when the offending symbol has no declaring syntax (metadata symbol). (derived)

## Notes from discussion

No comments on the issue. The reporter points at `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` being indexed unguarded at TypeCollector.cs lines 735, 1009 and 1101, and notes the neighbouring helpers use `FirstOrDefault()`. Possibly related: #2092 (CS8785 from the v3 generator, different inner exception, no repro).

hunches.claim: GetPropertyIdentifierLocation still indexes DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] unconditionally. For a closed generic metadata struct whose keyless property causes BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull to be created, the analyzer dereferences an empty syntax-reference collection and throws IndexOutOfRangeException before ReportIfLocatedInCompilation can drop the diagnostic. The AD0001 crash is not fully fixed.

receipt_plan.detail: Run Receipts.GeneratedTests.MetadataGenericStructDiagnosticsReceipts.KeylessPropertyOnMetadataGenericStructDoesNotCrashGeneratorOrAnalyzers. It references a separately compiled Lib.Item<T> [MessagePackObject] struct with a keyless Value property and uses Item<int> from an app-level [MessagePackObject]. On head, MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer reaches GetPropertyIdentifierLocation with no declaring syntax and the test fails with AD0001/IndexOutOfRangeException.

hunches.claim: The new GetPropertyIdentifierLocation helper still indexes DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0], so the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic path can still throw IndexOutOfRangeException for a property on a metadata-only closed generic struct. This leaves the reported generator/analyzer crash reachable despite the helper's documentation claiming metadata support.

receipt_plan.detail: Build the two-project repro with lib declaring [MessagePackObject] public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(null)] string Value); and app declaring a [MessagePackObject] type with an Item<int> member. Run both MessagePackGenerator and MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer and assert no CS8785 or AD0001 occurs and that app contains GeneratedMessagePackResolver; the current helper indexes the empty DeclaringSyntaxReferences collection when reporting BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull.

hunches.claim: The new GetPropertyIdentifierLocation helper still indexes DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0], so the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull path continues to throw for metadata properties. Its XML documentation promises a null result for metadata declarations, but the implementation does not provide it; the new UnkeyedMember repro exercises this crash rather than fixing it. Use FirstOrDefault and null propagation as in the neighbouring helpers.

receipt_plan.detail: Run ClosedGenericStruct_FromMetadataReference_UnkeyedMember. It calls the helper for the unkeyed metadata property; with the current implementation, DeclaringSyntaxReferences is empty and the test fails with IndexOutOfRangeException instead of producing the resolver.

hunches.claim: The new metadata-location helper still indexes DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0], contrary to its contract, and none of the added tests exercises the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic path. A referenced generic struct with a null-keyed property can therefore still crash both entry points instead of satisfying the metadata-diagnostic requirement.

receipt_plan.detail: Add a metadata-reference test whose generic struct property has [Key(null)], use that closed struct as a member in the usage compilation, run the analyzer and generator, and assert no AD0001/CS8785 plus generation of the resolver; the current helper throws IndexOutOfRangeException when the diagnostic is constructed.

hunches.claim: The added negative-only tests do not verify that the new diagnostic filter preserves diagnostics for symbols in the current compilation; inverting its condition would suppress all analyzer diagnostics while every added test still passes.

receipt_plan.detail: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:1445 negate-condition: diagnostic.Location.IsInSource && this.compilation.ContainsSyntaxTree(diagnostic.Location.SourceTree) -> !(diagnostic.Location.IsInSource && this.compilation.ContainsSyntaxTree(diagnostic.Location.SourceTree)); expected to survive because the added tests assert only absence of diagnostics and resolver generation, with no positive assertion that a source-located diagnostic is still reported.

hunches.claim: suppressed by unconfirmed context entry: [L8] area=analyzer, generator: Types that come from a referenced assembly are deliberately not analysed and get no formatter from the compiling assembly. In `TypeCollector.CollectCore`, after the custom-formatter, enum and generic checks, a non-generic type whose symbol is metadata-only exits with a bare `if (type.Locations[0].IsInMetadata) { return; }` (TypeCollector.cs:367-370), so no MsgPack003/004/005 diagnostic and no generated formatter appear for it. The defining assembly owns validating and formatting its own types (rationale inferred: the code has no comment). A missing diagnostic or formatter for such a type is not a defect. (source: src/MessagePack.SourceGenerator/CodeAnalysis/TypeCollector.cs:367) (would-be finding: Suppressing diagnostics for members of types from referenced assemblies is deliberate and matches the newly added documentation: the defining assembly owns those diagnostics. This should not be reversed merely because the consuming compilation no longer reports them.)

receipt_plan.detail: [L8] records that referenced-assembly types are deliberately not analysed and receive no MsgPack003/004/005 diagnostics from the compiling assembly; the defining assembly owns validation.
